correctness.rationale: Exact complete-bipartite shortest-path enumeration gives independent uniform opposite-side midpoint draws. Inclusion-exclusion supplies finite formula. Falling factorial moments equal (N-a)_r(1-r/N)^m, proving two independent Poisson limits; second moment / Markov proves sharp first-order thresholds; deterministic capacity follows from assigning one route per missing midpoint. A standalone graph-geodesic checker exhaustively cross-checks 47 finite triples and the exact probability formula. Finite enumeration is only supporting evidence; infinite statements proved symbolically.

value.rationale: Natural network/path-covering reliability problem: selecting a minimum strong geodetic set permits choosing paths, but independently uniform shortest-path choices need a larger terminal budget. The exact all-size law and sharp Poisson window quantify a multiplicative sqrt(log N) randomized-routing penalty, a distinction invisible in deterministic strong-geodetic numbers. The result is a motivated stochastic graph parameter rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice; classical coupon-collector machinery is acknowledged.
